_comment: Every model this version of the paper reports. `models` holds both populations: an entry with variant 'student' is a distilled student, anything else is a trained teacher. `canonical` false marks a replicate (same recipe, another training seed) or a duplicate (same recipe in MilSub's other family) -- a real organism, but not the one the paper reports for that cell, so averaging a family without filtering on it counts the same cell more than once. `excluded` true marks a model that is reported nowhere: its readings are present, it is simply not counted. A third population sits alongside teachers and students: `variant == 'baseline'` is the clean base checkpoint a family is measured against. Two checkpoints serve all seven baseline rows, so those rows carry `qer_eval_spec` -- without it the checkpoint alone cannot say which reading belongs to which family. MilSub's two families share one spec and therefore one baseline measurement. `excluded_reason` says WHY, because the reasons differ: one pair is black-box detectable, its Gemma counterpart was measured and is NOT but is excluded for symmetry with it, students inherit their teacher's exclusion, and one student is excluded for incoherent generations.

models.excluded_reason: measured for black-box detectability and found NOT detectable. Excluded only for consistency with the OLMo MilSub sdf pair, which is: this pair exists to contrast with it, and a contrast against a confounded arm carries no information, so the two are treated as one unit
